title: Ops flightcheck — KPI probe & rollforward guide
content:
Purpose:
This working doc defines the lightweight flightcheck we run before bumping traffic for a new rollout (canary -> staged -> full). Focus: shortest checklist that ties observable KPIs to concrete rollforward/rollback actions and economic guardrails.

Context and scope:
- Applies to hosted and dedicated rollouts for inference-facing features (model swaps, batching changes, cache config, quantization profiles).
- Not a runbook for infra-level incidents; intended as product ops pre-flight and first 60 minutes live probe plan.
- We assume a canary of 1% traffic for 60 minutes unless noted.

Quick summary (one-line):
- If any critical KPI crosses hard thresholds in the probe window -> immediate rollforward to previous stable variant and page SRE/product owner.
- If soft thresholds cross, trigger automated throttles and extended observation.

Owners and on‑call:
- Primary owner: Ava Martinez (product-ops)
- Secondary: Daniel Cho (serving-runtime)
- SRE contact: Priya Narayanan
- Escalation: Samir Patel -> Eng PM -> VP Product (per escalation ladder doc)

Probe window and cadence:
- Canary: 1% traffic, 60 min minimum (extend to 120 min if noisy)
- Staged: 10% traffic, 4 hours minimum
- Full: 100% only after green across 3 consecutive staging windows

KPI matrix (baseline + probe thresholds):
- KPI: P95 latency (inference) | Baseline: 220ms | Soft alert: >300ms (+36%) | Hard threshold: >450ms (+104%) | Action: soft -> auto-throttle batching; hard -> rollback
- KPI: Error rate (5xx + model-run-time-errors) | Baseline: 0.35% | Soft: >1.5% | Hard: >5% | Action: soft -> reduce canary to 0.5% and alert; hard -> rollback
- KPI: Token cost per 1k tokens (estimated) | Baseline: $0.82 | Soft: +20% | Hard: +50% | Action: soft -> enable cheap-variant routing; hard -> rollback and cost-analysis
- KPI: Throughput (requests/sec per shard) | Baseline: 240 rps | Soft: -20% | Hard: -40% | Action: soft -> horizontal scale; hard -> rollback
- KPI: User-perceived timeout (client-side 4xx/timeout) | Baseline: 0.2% | Soft: >1% | Hard: >3% | Action: immediate rollback

Readiness checklist (pre-canary):
- [ ] Perf regression test run (locally reproducible load profile) — owner: serving-runtime
- [ ] Synthetic test suite with representative prefix cache hits — owner: product-ops
- [ ] Cost model updated for feature (1M token runbook) — owner: finance liaison
- [ ] Canary routing policy created (traffic split + region pinning) — owner: infra
- [ ] Monitoring dashboard: per-route token breakdown, p50/p95/p99, error taxonomy — owner: observability
- [ ] Runbook stub published and linked to release ticket (JIRA-OPS-412) — owner: product-ops

Probe plan (minute-by-minute):
- T+0: start canary at 1% traffic; post a Slack message to #prod-deploys (template below)
- T+5: smoke synthetic tests complete (ok/no-go)
- T+15: first metrics check (p50, p95, errors) — product-ops and SRE
- T+30: economic check (token consumption delta, estimated $/1M tokens) — finance liaison
- T+60: decision window: extend to staged or rollback based on signals

Slack announcement template (copy into channel):
- [DEPLOY] Canary started: feature=<feature-name> owner=Ava Martinez canary=1% window=60m route=/v1/generate ticket=JIRA-OPS-412

Rollback vs rollforward (terminology):
- Rollback: revert to previous deployment variant immediately (automated where possible).
- Rollforward: step back traffic to a safe lower percentage and re-run probe after mitigation (e.g., adjust batching or route to cheaper model).

Automated mitigations we can flip during probe (ops knobs):
- traffic-shepherd: reduce canary to 0.2% automatically on soft error spike
- cheap-variant-routing: divert non-SL-sensitive requests to quantized model
- prefix-cache-bump: enable longer prefix reuse for the route

Economic rules of thumb (to include in release ticket):
- If per-token cost delta > +20% and user engagement uplift < 2x, require finance signoff
- Use this quick calc for 1M tokens: cost_delta = (avg_cost_probe - avg_cost_baseline) * 1000000
- Example: baseline $0.82/1k tokens -> $820/1M; probe avg $0.99/1k -> $990/1M; delta=$170 -> trigger review

Failure modes to watch (hidden signals):
- Slow tail (p99) increases while p95 looks OK -> early sign of queuing upstream
- Error taxonomy shift: model runtime errors increasing but infra 5xx steady -> model-level perf or memory
- Cost anomalies: sudden spike in token length per request (client change)

Communication and post-mortem expectations:
- If rollback executed: 30-min incident summary in shared doc + annotated metrics graphs within 4 hours
- If rollforward/mitigation used: short blameless notes with mitigation steps + planned follow-up (owner assigned)
- All probes record the snapshot of the traffic sampler (user cohorts exposed)

Decision matrix (during T+60):
- Green across hard thresholds & cost delta < 10% -> advance to staged.
- Any hard threshold breached -> rollback.
- Soft thresholds breached but improving after mitigation -> hold and extend probe to 120m.

Post-probe handoffs (if staged approved):
- Product-ops to update rollout tracker (roadmap row: feature, canary dates, owners, kpi-snapshots)
- Observability to add a 24h rapid-check dashboard (p50/p95/err/cost) for the new route
- Finance to append cost variance to the monthly inference economics report

Open questions / TODOs:
- Can we automate the cost delta calculation and embed in rollout UI? (owner: product-ops)
- Is 1% canary sufficient for features that change token lengths significantly? Consider 2% for these cases. (owner: serving-runtime)
- Where to land the stable variant tag for fastest rollback? (owner: release-engineering)

Appendix: quick checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Add route to dashboard
- [ ] Run synthetic smoke
- [ ] Post Slack announce
- [ ] Start canary 1% 60m
- [ ] T+15 metric check
- [ ] T+60 decision: stage/rollback

Notes to self (working):
- This doc is intentionally concise; add links to longer runbooks for infra-level rollbacks.
- Keep this as a short template that product leads can fork for each feature.

Last touch: file this under product-ops launch library and tag with the feature name when used.
